_comment: The capability table. This is the ONLY file that knows any vendor's flags.
The tick has no branch on runtime anywhere — a runtime is a row, not a code path.
The entry condition for being a first-class Smokin runtime is: it can be started by a
shell command, and it can write a file into a directory. It is NOT 'is one of herdr's
21 kinds' and NOT 'has a hook system'. Codewhale is neither and works fine.
{LINE} is the one-line dispatch prompt. {WT} is the plan root.
`env` is the ONLY place a vendor's environment variables are named, same rule as the
launch strings: a runtime is a row, not a code path. It exists because some rules cannot
survive as prose -- `Do NOT spawn sub-agents` sat in Grillin's task template as a line
nothing could check, and the caps below are the same rule in a form that cannot be
ignored. Keys must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ and values are shell-quoted where the pane
path builds a command; a key that does not match is dropped and named on the dispatch
record rather than silently applied. The record publishes the KEYS only -- a value can
be a token, and a dispatch record is readable by anyone who can read the plan.
`judge` is the command the delegation node uses for a tier-2 ruling, and it is the
only place {MODEL} and {EFFORT} are substituted. A runtime with no `judge` row falls
back to `headless`, which means the roster's pairing was REQUESTED and not applied —
and the ruling records that as pairing_enforced, rather than claiming a model that
never ran. A record that asserts an unapplied pairing is the defect class this whole
tool exists to catch, so it is not asserted.
EVERY LAUNCH STRING MUST BE WHITESPACE-SAFE. `launch()` builds argv as `head.split()`,
so `--output-format json` is fine and any flag whose VALUE contains a space is not —
it would arrive as two argv entries and the vendor would reject the second one.
`result_from` and `usage` — two readings of the transcript smokin-run already tees.
They exist because the ledger records events and timestamps, so wall-clock, retries
and first-pass verdict rate were derivable, and SPEND was not. Six agents were left
idle holding context a seventh pane was then opened to rebuild; nobody could say what
that cost, because nothing measured it.
result_from : {select, match, path}   which record carries the final assistant text
usage       : {select, match, map, cost_usd}   which record carries the numbers
select  'last' = the run total is already totalled by the vendor; take the last match
'sum'  = the vendor reports PER STEP and the run total is their sum
'join' = the vendor STREAMS the text in chunks (result_from only)
match   every key/value must equal, on the record; absent means any object
map     receipt key -> dotted path FROM THE RECORD ROOT. Not from a `usage` prefix:
claude puts tokens under .usage and cost at the top level, so no single
prefix addresses both, and a descriptor needing an escape hatch for its own
first runtime is the wrong descriptor.
COST IS NOT TOKENS AND THE TWO ARE NOT ONE CAPABILITY. `cost_usd` is declared only by
a runtime that actually reports one. codewhale reports tokens and no cost at all, so
its row has no cost_usd key and its receipts will never carry the field. The
alternative — a price table this repository invents — is an unearned assertion.
A row with NEITHER key is not broken. It is a runtime nobody has measured yet, its
receipts carry no `usage`, and that absence is the honest reading.

claude.env_note: THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS ARE FAR HIGHER THAN ANYONE EXPECTS, and that is the whole argument for this block. Read out of the installed bundle (@anthropic-ai/claude-code 2.1.263): CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS falls back to 20, and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH to 3. Twenty concurrent subagents, each able to spawn two levels further, is the behaviour a plan gets when nobody sets anything -- and a Claude 5 generation model delegates more readily than its predecessors, so the ceiling is likelier to be reached than it used to be. These four numbers are a JUDGMENT, not a measurement: nobody here has benchmarked 2-versus-4 concurrency on a real plan. What IS measured is what they replace. Depth 1 is the load-bearing one: it lets a task fan out once and stops the fan-out from fanning out, which is the shape that turns one task into an unbounded bill. MODEL_FORCE IS A SWITCH, NOT A MODEL, and this row said otherwise from 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-11: it read `claude-sonnet-5` and was described as pinning every subagent to Sonnet. Read out of the bundle, FORCE is only tested for being set -- it removes the Agent tool's `model` parameter -- and the model comes from CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, which was never set, so subagents inherited their parent. Now: FORCE is `1`, and `subagent_model_env` names the variable Smokin fills PER DISPATCH from the task's persona file `model:` or its **Model:** -- a Haiku persona's helpers run on Haiku, an Opus persona's on Opus, and neither can ask for another. Escalating is a change to the task's contract, where it is visible. Override any of them per project; delete the block and Claude Code's own defaults apply, which is the state this exists to leave.
claude.verified: installed at ~/.npm-global/bin/claude. `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format json "reply with the single word OK"` CONFIRMED: exit 0, ONE line of stdout, an envelope with type=result, result="OK", usage.input_tokens=2, usage.output_tokens=4, usage.cache_read_input_tokens=15989, usage.cache_creation_input_tokens=13486, total_cost_usd=0.1429645. The envelope being one line is why the scanner needs no separate whole-file mode. Also CONFIRMED through the full path — a one-task plan dispatched by `smokin run` returned terminal=ok, claim=done, `result` as PROSE (not the envelope), and usage={input_tokens:8, output_tokens:491, cache_read_tokens:107771, cache_write_tokens:15423, cost_usd:0.2204305} on both the receipt and the ledger.
claude.note: `judge` is deliberately NOT given --output-format json. The delegation node reads that command's stdout as prose and nothing in this change asked it to stop; changing a row nobody measured would be a preference, not a fix. A per-pane --settings accelerant is still NOT shipped: whether it merges or replaces is untested, and if it replaces it would silently disable herdr’s own state hook and Grillin’s awareness hooks. Open question Q3.

codewhale.verified: `codewhale exec --auto --output-format stream-json "reply with the single word OK"` CONFIRMED: exit 0, four NDJSON line types — content, session_capture, metadata, done — with meta.input_tokens=15315, meta.prompt_cache_hit_tokens=1792, meta.prompt_cache_miss_tokens=13523, meta.output_tokens=39, meta.reasoning_tokens=37, and NO cost field anywhere in the envelope. A second run ("count from one to twenty") CONFIRMED that `content` events are STREAMED TOKEN CHUNKS — ‘ele’ then ‘ven’ — which is why result_from joins them and does not take the last. Pane emission CONFIRMED separately by experiment Q1: the wrapper trap fires on pane close with rc=129.
codewhale.note: The declared `--json` summary was dropped because it carries no token field at all — a dead end confirmed twice, once with real tool use. It also means DESIGN §3f’s ‘Codewhale’s exec --json .output’ is no longer where `result` comes from; the joined content stream is. NO cost_usd key is declared here, and that is the point: codewhale reports tokens and nothing else, this repository has no price table, and inventing one to fill a column is the unearned assertion CONTRIBUTING refuses. `input_tokens` maps to prompt_cache_miss_tokens, NOT to meta.input_tokens — codewhale’s input_tokens is the TOTAL including cache hits (15315 = 1792 + 13523), whereas claude’s excludes them, and mapping the two onto one name would silently compare unlike things. Under the mapping used here, total input = input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens on every runtime that reports the parts. Not one of herdr’s 21 agent kinds, so herdr cannot classify its lifecycle. Under Smokin that costs nothing: the tick never asks herdr what any agent is doing. Its global-only hooks must never carry a task id — a hook is machine-wide and would fire for every pane.

opencode.verified: `opencode run --format json "reply with the single word OK"` CONFIRMED: exit 0, NDJSON on stdout with step_start / text / step_finish, part.tokens={total:8499,input:8497,output:2,reasoning:0,cache:{write:0,read:0}} and part.cost=0.003697935. A second run ("count from one to twenty") CONFIRMED that a `text` part arrives WHOLE — one event, 131 chars — not in chunks, which is why result_from takes the last and does not join. First invocation took over two minutes to print anything; that is server start-up, not a hang, and it matters because a budget under ~180s will reap this runtime before it speaks.
opencode.note: usage select is `sum`, not `last`: step_finish is emitted PER STEP, so a run with tool use reports several and the run total is their sum. claude and codewhale are `last` because their envelope already totals the run, and summing a repeated total would double it. Its SSE event stream needs a resident subscriber, which is the one thing this design refuses to depend on. Wrapper + reaper only.
